messages:
maria: Quick question on defining "goodput" in our bench docs — are we measuring tokens accepted by model per second or completed responses? I'm getting inconsistent numbers across replay vs synthetic runs.

jon: Good question. In my head goodput = completed output tokens/sec that pass postfiltering. But we historically used QPS * avg_tokens as a proxy. We need to pick one and stick to it.

rahul: FWIW, for TPOT/TTFT we need to separate request-level latency from token-level throughput. TTFT measures time to first token from request arrival. TPOT is tokens produced per second once stream starts, right?

alex: Correct. Also KV cache warm state complicates goodput — cache hits speed tokens but different harnesses warm the cache differently.

maria: So how do we normalize when comparing replay vs synthetic? synthetic often pads prompts and removes user think times, replay has real inter-arrival gaps.

jon: Suggest mapping the loadspace explicitly: define three axes — concurrency (parallel inflight requests), arrival pattern (poisson / bursty / recorded replay), and input-length distribution. Run the same matrix for both harnesses.

rahul: +1. Also include an explicit KV-warmup step in replay: run a fixed number of warm requests until cache-hit-rate stabilizes, then start measurement window.

alex: Proposed doc snippet to include in SOP:

```
loadspace:
  concurrency: [1, 4, 16, 64]
  arrival: ["poisson_1", "burst_10_1", "recorded_replay"]
  input_pcts: {"short": 0.6, "med": 0.3, "long": 0.1}
  kv_warmup: 5000
metrics:
  goodput: "completed_output_tokens / wall_time_excluding_warmup"
  qps: "requests_completed / wall_time"
  ttft_p50_p95_p99: "percentiles(time_from_request_start_to_first_token)"
  tpot: "tokens_generated_per_active_stream_avg"
```

alex: Also: standardize measurement windows, explicitly exclude warmup, and report cache-hit-rate per-input-bucket. Remove single-request outliers (e.g., >5x median) from percentile calc after flagging.

maria: Nice. Any objections to making goodput exclude responses with >20% server-side truncation?

jon: Makes sense — filter truncated completions and report them as a separate column. Also add a column for model-switch fallbacks.

bench-bot: run: `bench-run --profile loadspace_matrix.yaml --output results/2212345678.json` :white_check_mark:

rahul: I'll draft a PR to the benchmark SOP with these definitions and attach example plots (goodput vs concurrency, ttft CDF) :+1:

maria: Great — thanks everyone. Let's try a small calibration run tomorrow and merge the baseline if numbers look sane.
